content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have temperature sensors and would like to show their readings on the [product_name] display and in [product_name] web editor. My idea is to make the sensor's representation disappear in both places if I remove a sensor from the bus while the program is running. If I reconnect the sensor, it should reappear in both the web editor and display automatically. I want this behavior to be real-time—the value and the thermometer should vanish upon removal, and reappear upon reconnection. Currently, removing a sensor results in a reading of -127°C, which I'd prefer to hide rather than display. Are there any tips or methods to dynamically show or hide elements in the [product_name] web editor or display based on sensor readings? Thank you very much.
One approach is to add a rectangle over the display, which can be shown only when you do not want to see the sensor value.

So is it possible to show or hide the rectangle depending on the value received? For example, if the reading is -127.00, display the rectangle, correct? Is this not possible on the [product_name] display?
The [product_name] display and the web server are quite different. The display is text-based, while the web editor is graphics-based. It's like comparing two things with distinct functions.

I haven't been able to set up a rectangle to display only when I want. To show normal temperature, the rectangle needs to be transparent over the value, but I haven't found any transparent images in the web editor. Also, if I could remove the option to display an image when the digital value is '0', I could show the rectangle only with '1'. Do you have any suggestions for hiding images with '0' or making them transparent? Thank you!

You need two images: one matching the background color and one transparent. Use a digital value to select which to display—if it's 0, show the transparent image; if 1, use the background image. I've attached a transparent example.
I've included a small example in the attachment.

analysis.insight_summary: Users wish to dynamically control sensor visualization in both the [product_name] web editor and display, preferring invisible graphics or placeholders over showing faulty readings like -127°C when sensors are disconnected. However, differing design constraints between the text-based display and the graphic-based web editor make this challenging and cause user confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect sensor visualizations to automatically disappear or become invisible in both the [product_name] display and web editor when sensors are unplugged, and reappear when reconnected, avoiding confusing placeholder values.
